title: Saturation and pile-up joint energy recovery with censored waveform targets
claimed_ticket_title: S38b: saturation and pile-up joint energy recovery with censored waveform targets
claimed_ticket_body: Question: can models recover charge/energy proxies from saturated or overlapping pulses better than conservative censored traditional reconstruction? Compare a traditional clipped-template integral plus two-pulse bounded fit against ridge, gradient-boosted trees, MLP, 1D-CNN, and a masked-token waveform transformer on duplicate-readout, injected pile-up, and run-heldout saturation slices. Require bootstrap CIs for charge residual, energy-proxy bias, timing shift, pile-up false split/merge rate, saturation-onset calibration, and PID-proxy migration. Expected information gain: maps the boundary where pulse-shape learning adds usable energy information versus absorbing pile-up or saturation artifacts.

evaluation_design.split: train and held-out sets are disjoint by source run
evaluation_design.negative_control: clean single-pulse controls with matched source-run distribution
evaluation_design.pid_proxy_migration: span of median energy residual across B2/B4/B6/B8 staves

winner.name: template_residual_boosted_stack_new
winner.criterion: minimum held-out composite saturation-energy/timing score with run-block and injection-source bootstrap CIs reported

caveats: Truth comes from controlled injections into raw-ROOT-derived clean pulses.
Saturation is represented by an amplitude-ceiling proxy rather than electronics saturation flags.
Injection-source cells are retained provenance units, not exact residual waveform indices.
